question: Which of the following crops is NOT grown during the Zaid season in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rice**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Rice is typically grown during the Kharif season (June to November) and Rabi season (November to March) in India.
 
• The Zaid season falls between the Rabi and Kharif seasons, specifically from March to June.
 
• Crops like cucumber, watermelon, and muskmelon are commonly grown during the Zaid season due to their shorter growing period and summer adaptability.
 
• Rice requires a significant amount of water and is usually grown in areas with assured irrigation during the monsoon season (Kharif) or post-monsoon season (Rabi).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kharif Season**

 
 
• The Kharif season is also known as the monsoon season, running from June to November.
 
• Crops grown during this season are typically sown with the beginning of the first rains in July, during the south-west monsoon season, and harvested in October.
 
• Major Kharif crops include rice, maize, sorghum, pearl millet, and cotton.
 
 
 
• **Rabi Season**
 
 
• The Rabi season is known as the winter season, running from November to March.
 
• Crops are sown in winter and harvested in the spring.
 
• Major Rabi crops include wheat, barley, peas, gram, and mustard.
 
 
 
• **Zaid Season**
 
 
• The Zaid season falls between the Kharif and Rabi seasons, specifically from March to June.
 
• Crops grown during this season have a shorter growing period and are typically summer crops.
 
• Examples of Zaid crops include cucumber, watermelon, muskmelon, and bitter gourd.
 
 

This detailed solution provides comprehensive information about the correct option and explains the different agricultural seasons in India
